visual_action: The video opens with a wide shot of a large protest crowd in front of the U.S. Supreme Court building. It then transitions to a montage of still photographs of individual protesters and small groups of protesters, mostly women of various ages and ethnicities, holding handmade signs advocating for abortion rights.

cast.name: Democratic Party
cast.evidence: The first frame of the video has overlay text that reads "Democrats support REPRODUCTIVE RIGHTS FOR ALL".

cast.name: Ruth Bader Ginsburg
cast.evidence: The video's audio begins with a recording of her famous quote: "All I ask of our brethren is that they take their feet off our necks."

cast.name: Thomas Jefferson
cast.evidence: A protest sign attributes the quote "The dead cannot bind the living" to "- Jefferson".

cast.name: Brett Kavanaugh
cast.evidence: A protest sign attributes the quote "I like beer" to "- Kavanaugh".

cast.name: Supreme Court of the United States
cast.evidence: The protest is shown taking place directly in front of the Supreme Court building.

spoken_summary: The video begins with an audio clip of Ruth Bader Ginsburg saying, "All I ask of our brethren is that they take their feet off our necks." The rest of the audio is a song.
audio_music: The video starts with a spoken word quote for the first ~6 seconds. Then, an anthemic and empowering pop song, identified as Sia's "Unstoppable," begins and plays for the remainder of the video, accompanying the montage of protesters. The song's tone is one of determination and resilience.
editing_pacing: The video consists of a single wide shot followed by a slideshow of still photographs, with simple cuts between each image.
cultural_references: The song "Unstoppable" by Sia is featured prominently.
A protest sign parodies the lyrics of Carly Rae Jepsen's song "Call Me Maybe".
central_claim: The Democratic Party supports reproductive rights for all people and stands in solidarity with those protesting to protect them.
intended_effect: To align the Democratic Party with the pro-choice movement, energize supporters, and convey a message of strength and unity on the issue of abortion rights.
